message.reasoning:
I'm setting up a TokenTest class in the org.jsoup.parser package to access the package-private Token class and its nested types, planning coverage for Doctype fields and the various branches in Tag's newAttribute logic.

Extending that out, I need tests for finaliseTag, name(), isSelfClosing, getAttributes, the appendTagName/appendAttributeName/appendAttributeValue methods for both String and char overloads, the StartTag/EndTag constructors and toString variants, plus Comment, Character, EOF, and the type-check/cast methods like isDoctype/asDoctype across all token types, along with tokenType(). I'm also noting that Token has a private constructor, so I need to figure out how its subclasses can actually extend it despite that restriction.

Private members in Java are accessible within the enclosing top-level class and all its nested classes, since Token's subclasses are nested within Token.java itself, so the private constructor works fine there. I can instantiate Doctype, StartTag, EndTag, Comment, Character, and EOF directly since they're package-private or public static nested classes in the same package as my test.

Now I'm writing out the full JUnit4 test, covering the newAttribute branches: calling it with both attributes and pendingAttributeName null, calling it after appendAttributeName only (value defaults to empty string), and calling it after both appendAttributeName and appendAttributeValue are set.

Since pendingAttributeValue and pendingAttributeName are private, I need to test their reset behavior indirectly through public methods like getAttributes() after finaliseTag, verifying that repeated appendAttributeValue calls accumulate correctly and reset properly between attributes. I'm also planning to use StartTag (which initializes attributes in its constructor) versus EndTag (which leaves attributes null until the first newAttribute call) to cover both the null and non-null attributes branches, starting with a basic test asserting Doctype's default field values.

I also want to verify that appending directly to the package-private StringBuilder fields works as expected, and then check what happens when name() is called on a StartTag whose tagName was never initialized—since tagName.length() on a null field would throw a NullPointerException rather than the expected IllegalArgumentException, which is worth testing as actual behavior rather than assumption.

Since this is part of the same project (Defects4J Jsoup-31b), the jsoup classes themselves should already be compiled and available without needing a separate jar import.

I'll trust that Validate.isFalse(true) throws an IllegalArgumentException based on standard jsoup behavior. For the remaining tests: testNameSetterAndGetter checks that setting a name on a StartTag correctly updates both the name() getter and tagName field, while testAppendTagNameWhenNull verifies behavior when an EndTag's tagName is null by default.

I'm covering the appendTagName branches - testing concatenation when tagName already has a value, testing the char overload delegates to the string version, and testing appendAttributeName both when pendingAttributeName starts null (sets it directly) and when it already has content (concatenates).

I'm continuing through the remaining attribute tests - value concatenation mirrors the name logic, char overloads delegate similarly, and the newAttribute cases verify attributes collection gets lazily initialized and populated correctly whether or not a pending name exists.

Since the second call's pendingAttributeValue is empty but not null, it ends up adding attribute b="" rather than skipping it, so I need to verify size equals 2 with that empty value. Then I'm checking finaliseTag behavior with and without a pending attribute name, confirming it adds the attribute when a name is pending and does nothing when there isn't one.

I also want to confirm self-closing defaults to false until explicitly set, verify the constructors behave correctly, and think through how toString should render attributes without locking into an exact string format since the underlying Attributes.toString() output isn't fully certain -- better to check for key substrings like the tag opening and closing rather than an exact match.

Then I'm outlining tests for EndTag and Comment toString behavior, plus starting to think through Character node data retrieval.

Next I plan EOF token tests checking its type and isEOF flag, then a broader set of type-check tests verifying each token's isXxx/asXxx methods behave correctly against their own type and return false/null for mismatched types.

token type returns getClass().getSimpleName(), so a StartTag's tokenType() should equal "StartTag".

25. testAsDoctypeCastException - casting a StartTag via asDoctype() should throw ClassCastException, good for at least one mismatch test.

I'll keep the test set reasonable rather than exhaustive, covering the branches mentioned. I'll need to import Attributes/Attribute from org.jsoup.nodes for building attributes, assuming the standard jsoup API's put(String key, String value) method exists even though it's not shown in the provided source.

I'm also planning to directly test appendAttributeName(char) and appendAttributeValue(char) by calling them and verifying the resulting attributes. For the final code, I need the correct package and imports—org.jsoup.parser, JUnit's Test and Assert, plus the nested Token subclasses (Doctype, StartTag, etc.), which are package-private but accessible since the test class lives in the same package. Now I'm writing the final test code, handling expected exceptions carefully.

I'm confirming Validate.isFalse throws an IllegalArgumentException when the value is true, matching jsoup's standard implementation, so I'll use that exception type in assertions. I also need to remember that tagName and attributes fields are accessible directly within the package since they're protected or package-private, but pendingAttributeName and pendingAttributeValue are private and not directly reachable.
